screens.prompt: In B10, count how many tickets have the status "Open".

hints.syntax: The criterion is text, so it goes in quotes: =COUNTIF(B2:B9,"Open").
hints.func-countif: COUNTIF counts the rows that match a condition. COUNT only counts numbers, and this column holds words.
hints.require-ref: The first argument points at the status column, not at the answer cell.
hints.value: The count is short by one. Check that the range reaches B9, where the last ticket sits.
hints.error: Unquoted criteria is read as a name, so the cell shows #NAME? instead of a number.

reject.why: range stops one row short, so the last Open ticket is missed
COUNT counts non-empty cells, not ones that match
points at the ticket IDs instead of the status column
unquoted criteria is read as a name

docs.explain:
COUNTIF reads a range and counts the cells that meet one condition. Text criteria go in quotes, so =COUNTIF(B2:B9,"Open") returns 4: four of the eight statuses read Open. A number needs no quotes, while ">=5" and "<>Closed" keep theirs because a comparison is still text.

This sheet holds eight tickets with four different statuses, and the answer sits under the last of them. The range has to reach B9. Stop at B8 and the count comes back as 3, one short, and the ticket you missed is not marked.

Case does not matter, so "open" and "Open" land in the same count. Wildcards work inside the criteria as well: "O*" also returns 4 here, and "T-10*" tested against column A would count all eight tickets.

errors.text: An unquoted criterion such as COUNTIF(B2:B9,Open) sends Excel looking for a name called Open, and there is none.
A range that stops at B8 counts three Open tickets and reports nothing wrong.
The range points at cells that have been deleted since, so there is nothing left to count.

docs.atWork: Support queues and stock rooms run on this count: how many tickets are open, how many lines are short. It is just as often tallied by eye, one screen at a time.
docs.outcome: Count the rows that meet one condition, and get the edges of the range right.

seo.title: COUNTIF in Excel: count rows that match
seo.description: COUNTIF counts the rows that meet one condition. Four of these eight tickets read Open, so the formula returns 4, and the criteria syntax is the lesson.
